story.text: The Duchess {FLINGS} the baby to Alice and hurries off to play croquet. Alice carries it out into the open {AIR}, but it {GRUNTS}, and its nose turns up like a {SNOUT}. There is no mistake about it: it is a {PIG}! She sets it down, and it trots quietly {AWAY}. If it had grown up, she thinks, it would have made a dreadfully ugly child: “but it makes rather a {HANDSOME} pig.”
story.caption: It was neither more nor less than a pig
story.credit: John Tenniel, coloured for The Nursery “Alice”, 1890
